subject: Post-discovery: evaluation plan, model recommendations & rollback policy
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acmepay.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmepay.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 22:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-discovery: evaluation plan, model recommendations & rollback policy

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run the evaluation pack:

- Goal: validate model fit for AcmePay’s customer support triage + payment dispute summarization flows (priority: triage).
- Success metrics: F1-ish qualitative pass on categorization benchmarks (>88% by your in-house labels), concise extractive summaries w/ ROUGE-L > 0.55 on the test set we discussed.
- Recommended models to include in the eval: gpt-small-8k-quantized, redwood-3b-v2, redwood-13b-q4 (we’ll include a float baseline for latency comparisons).

Attachments: I’ve attached the evaluation pack (acme_eval_pack_v1.zip) and the prompt set we’ll run (prompt_set_acmepay_v2.csv). Benchmark results template is attached for your review.

Risk callout: you mentioned concerns about output regressions after model updates. Our recommended safety net for the trial:
  1) Pin the trial traffic to a specific model version (we suggest redwood-13b-q4@2027-05-01) while running the eval,
  2) Run the eval against both the pinned version and the latest candidate; if any regression >5% on key metrics, we automatically revert live traffic to the pinned version,
  3) We’ll keep a 24-hour rolling window where ad-hoc rollbacks are possible and annotate all rollbacks in the audit logs you’ll get in the console.

Proposed timeline:
- Mon 24 May: we ship the eval pack and kickoff automated runs from our side (you can run locally if you prefer).
- Tue 25 May: preliminary benchmark report + latency/vs-cost delta.
- Wed 26 May: sync to review diffs and agree pin/rollback.

Next steps for you: please confirm the list of internal labels we should use (you mentioned "priority, routing, dispute_type") and confirm you’re comfortable with the suggested pin window and rollback policy.

If you’re good, I’ll loop in Aditya (ML eng) and Marissa (CS lead) to own the execution and monitoring.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@acmepay.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmepay.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: evaluation plan, model recommendations & rollback policy

Thanks Markus — helpful recap. A couple quick notes: 

- Labels: confirm we’ll supply the "priority" and "dispute_type" columns; we also want an "escalation_required" flag added to the prompts so the triage model can surface when to route to refunds ops.
- Pin/rollback: the automatic rollback threshold sounds reasonable but can we narrow the metric to two primary KPIs (categorization accuracy and summary compression ratio) — those are the only ones the business will accept as regression triggers.
- Timing: tight timeline but we can aim for the Mon kickoff; I’ll ask engineering to give us a small VM to run the pack if you need local runs.

Also: curious if you can include a small adversarial prompt set (we saw odd behavior in another vendor trial) — would like to see stability there.

Samir
Product Ops Lead, AcmePay
samir.k@acmepay.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acmepay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmepay.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: evaluation plan, model recommendations & rollback policy

Sounds good — looping in Aditya and Marissa. Aditya: can your runbook cover the following?

- Include the adversarial prompt set Samir requested (I’ve added a small set to prompt_set_acmepay_v2.csv and flagged the examples).
- Run the eval pack against: redwood-13b-q4@2027-05-01 (pinned baseline), redwood-13b-q4@canary (latest candidate), gpt-small-8k-quantized.
- Produce a diff report that highlights: per-label precision/recall, summary length distribution, top-10 tokens changed in logits for disputed examples, and a simple human-review checklist for any failing examples.
- If candidate shows >5 percentage point drop on either categorization accuracy or summary compression ratio (we’ll compute compression ratio as summary_length/reference_length), trigger the auto-rollback flag and open a rollback incident ticket.

Marissa: can CS prep a short walkthrough for Samir’s team the day after preliminary results land? I suggest a 30-minute session to go through failing examples and confirm business impact.

Samir — we’ll start the automated runs now and share preliminary artifacts to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1A2B3C4D5E6F (attached the initial benchmark_report_20270522.html).

Attaching: acme_eval_pack_v1.zip, prompt_set_acmepay_v2.csv, benchmark_report_20270522.html

— Markus

That all looks good — thank you for the clear plan and for adding the adversarial set. We approve the pinned baseline and the rollback thresholds focused on the two KPIs discussed.

Please proceed with the runs. Ellen and I will sit in on the Wed diff review if possible.

Samir
Product Ops Lead, AcmePay
